sections.html:
Across the Savannah River from Augusta, Georgia, North Augusta occupies the river's north bank. Most of it lies in western Aiken County, but a small northern piece belongs to Edgefield County. That split matters because your parcel's county determines who bills the property tax. City government is a mayor-council system with seven council members, so permit and code questions go to city hall rather than the county.

A land company formed in the 1890s started the city, and incorporation followed on April 11, 1906. Growth linked to the Savannah River Plant later nearly quadrupled the population and enlarged the city from 772 acres to 5,139 acres.

That history left early twentieth century streets sitting beside postwar subdivisions. Part of the Georgia Avenue and Butler Avenue Historic District is on the National Register of Historic Places, so owners there should phone the city before planning any exterior change.

Most students attend Aiken County Public Schools, and the part of the city in Edgefield County is served by the Edgefield County School District. Many families also send children to private schools across the river in Georgia. North Augusta High School and Fox Creek High School, an independent charter school, are the high schools.

The Thirteen Street bridge, also called the James U. Jackson Memorial Bridge, carries traffic across the Savannah River to Augusta. Greeneway Trail, established in 1995, adds more than 9 miles of paved trail on a former railroad line, and SRP Park on the river is home to the Augusta GreenJackets.

One parcel can receive two bills on different calendars. The city's tax is due May 1, and a 15 percent penalty is added afterward. Aiken County mails real property bills in the fall, payable without penalty through January 16, and adds penalties in January, February and March.

State law frames the general window as September 30 through January 15, with penalty steps of 3, 7 and 5 percent. Since the two schedules do not line up, look at both bills before closing and verify any amount with the Aiken County Treasurer's office.

sections.h2: Delinquent taxes and the November tax sale
sections.html:
Overdue accounts pass to the Delinquent Tax Collector, whose office is in Suite 2500 of the Government Center, 1930 University Parkway, Aiken. The property itself can be sold. North Augusta runs its yearly tax sale together with Aiken County on the first Monday in November.

Old balances have to be cleared before current ones will be accepted, and collection costs keep accruing. Back taxes headed toward that sale deserve action now: either pay them or close before the date. A title company will insist on a clean record at closing.

sections.h2: How Aiken County assesses a house
sections.html:
Owner-occupied homes are taxed at 4 percent of value instead of 6 percent, and an owner may claim that rate on one legal residence in South Carolina. Rentals, second homes, commercial property and land over five acres may not qualify.

The assessor's FAQ points to two facts that matter at a sale. Reappraisal increases are capped at 15 percent of the base-year value, with 2007 as the base year. When an assessable transfer happens, though, the county may set value at current market value and skip the cap.

So a buyer may face a larger bill than you paid, and it is fair to say so up front. If you want to contest a value, call the assessor at the Government Center and ask for the current deadline.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Aiken County
sections.html:
A North Augusta deed in Aiken County is filed with the Register of Deeds, Suite 2100 of the Government Center, 1930 University Parkway, Aiken, phone 803.642.2072. Staff do not run title searches, give legal advice or prepare forms. If your parcel is in Edgefield County, record it there.

Electronic images exist for documents recorded after June 12, 2005, though they can be viewed only on computers inside the office. Earlier documents sit in books.

A transfer fee applies on top of recording charges: $1.85 per $500 of value, of which $1.30 goes to the state and $0.55 to the county. Estate deeds of distribution do not owe it, a break for heirs.

An owner must give a buyer a written property condition disclosure unless the transfer is exempt. Fiduciary sales by an estate, a foreclosure and an agreed written waiver are among the exemptions, and as-is agreements remain allowed. The rules are in Title 27, Chapter 50.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
• Find your parcel's county on the last tax bill, since Aiken and Edgefield handle bills and deeds separately.
  • Pull both the city bill and the county bill and note which are paid.
  • Ask city hall about open permits or code issues, because the city, not the county, handles them.
  • If the house is older, learn whether it falls inside the historic district before you promise a buyer any exterior work.

None of this takes long, and it keeps a buyer's attorney from finding surprises you could have explained yourself.

sections.h2: When owners choose a cash sale
sections.html:
North Augusta owners tend to compare cash against listing when they face one of these:

  • Deferred repairs that would stall a bank appraisal
  • An inherited home with heirs living out of state
  • Back taxes that are drifting toward the November tax sale
  • A rental they are done managing

Cash Home Buyers reviews North Augusta houses in the shape they are in and writes up any offer. We cannot promise one for every property. Put what we send next to a listing plan and then decide.

sections.h2: What happens after you say yes
sections.html:
Next comes a closing date of your choosing. Since no lender is part of the deal, no appraisal holds things up, and the schedule follows the title search and any payoffs. The title company verifies ownership, settles your mortgage and any tax balance out of the proceeds, and files the deed in the correct county.

At the first call, have recent bills from the city and the county, a payoff figure for any loan and, for an inherited house, the papers naming who may sign. A parcel that touches a county line should be flagged right away.

Plan for the last stretch as well: transfer utilities, hand over keys and garage openers at closing, and keep copies of the settlement papers for your records.

faqs.q: What county is North Augusta in?
faqs.a: Mostly Aiken County, with a small part in Edgefield County. Your parcel's county decides who bills your property tax and where you record your deed.

faqs.q: When are North Augusta property taxes due?
faqs.a: The city's tax is due May 1 with a 15 percent penalty afterward. Aiken County real property bills are payable without penalty by January 16. Confirm both before closing.

faqs.q: When is the Aiken County tax sale?
faqs.a: North Augusta holds its annual tax sale with Aiken County on the first Monday in November.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a North Augusta house?
faqs.a: In Aiken County, it goes to the Register of Deeds at 1930 University Parkway, Suite 2100, Aiken. Call 803.642.2072 to confirm requirements. Edgefield County parcels go to that county.

faqs.q: Will a buyer pay the same property tax I did?
faqs.a: Not always. In Aiken County an assessable transfer lets the value reset to current market value instead of being held by the 15 percent cap, so the new bill can rise.
